# Change Timezone in Laravel: Beyond the config/app.php Trap

If you are attempting to switch your Laravel application from UTC to a specific region like `Asia/Tehran`, it is common to head straight for `config/app.php`. The logic seems sound: locate the `'timezone'` configuration line and swap the value. In your case, changing it from `'UTC'` to `'Asia/Tehran'` followed by clearing caches often yields no change in behavior. This frustration stems from a fundamental misunderstanding of how Laravel handles timezones at different architectural layers.

The `app.php` file controls the application's internal default timezone, which primarily affects functions that rely on PHP's global timezone setting or specific Eloquent date helpers when called without explicit parameters. However, simply editing this configuration does not automatically shift the output for all views or API responses if other components are overriding it. You must identify where the actual rendering logic resides and ensure consistency across the stack.

To persistently change the application-wide default, you must update `config/app.php` as you attempted, but then explicitly enforce that setting in your view rendering context. If you are using Blade templates, simply changing the config is insufficient if your views contain raw PHP time functions or if your API controllers rely on server-side formatting without passing a timezone argument. The most robust approach is to set the default timezone at the very beginning of your application lifecycle.

You can enforce this by modifying `bootstrap/app.php` (in Laravel 9+) or `app/bootstrap/app.php`. Add the following line near the top of the file, before any other configuration is loaded:

```php
date_default_timezone_set('Asia/Tehran');
```

This command operates at the PHP core level, ensuring that every function relying on the system timezoneâsuch as `date()`, `time()`, or `DateTime` constructors without argumentsâuses `Asia/Tehran`. This is critical because Laravel's time helpers like `now()` or `Carbon::now()` default to the server's timezone if no offset is provided. By setting the global PHP timezone early, you guarantee that these defaults align with your intended output without needing to manually pass `'Asia/Tehran'` into every single query or view snippet.

However, relying solely on this global setting introduces a significant trade-off: it couples your application logic to a specific geographical location. If you plan to serve users globally, hardcoding `Asia/Tehran` in the core configuration will display incorrect local times for users in Europe or North America. For instance, a user in London expecting `2023-10-27 14:00` might see `2023-10-27 16:00` if your application defaults to Tehran time without context.

The recommended architectural pattern is to keep the `config/app.php` value as a fallback and rely on Carbon's built-in timezone detection or explicit parameter passing in critical paths. You can configure the default in `app.php` while ensuring your models and controllers explicitly handle offsets when necessary. For example, when saving timestamps to the database, Laravel defaults to UTC regardless of the `timezone` setting in `app.php`. This is by design for data integrity across regions. If you change `config/app.php`, remember that stored values remain in UTC; only the display layer changes based on your configuration or Carbon's `now()` behavior.

If you require a dynamic solution where different users see their local times, avoid global overrides. Instead, use middleware to inject the user's preferred timezone into the request context or rely on database-stored timezone preferences. This approach prevents the pitfalls of a one-size-fits-all configuration that breaks international deployments. When in doubt, verify your output using `dd(Carbon::now())` within a route to confirm whether the change is taking effect at the display layer versus the data storage layer.

For further guidance on managing dates and times efficiently within the Laravel ecosystem, including best practices for handling timezone offsets and Carbon instances, visit https://laravelcompany.com.
